title: Steve Jobs at Palo Alto High School, 1996: Be creative, don't be a career, blaze while you're in the sky
summary: In a 1996 graduation speech, Jobs urges students to trust their intuitions, gather diverse experiences so they can connect dots others miss, and refuse the "career" in favor of making what they love their work. He frames life as a rainbow where the journey is the reward, and mortality as the reason to blaze.

principles.text: Creativity is connecting experiences others don't see, so you must gather diverse experiences off the beaten path.
principles.quote: Creativity equals connecting previously unrelated experiences and insights that others don’t see.

principles.text: Follow curiosity even with no obvious payoff; the dots connect later, as calligraphy did for the Mac.
principles.quote: The only thing one can do is to believe that some of what you follow with your heart will indeed come back to make your life much richer.

principles.text: Don't treat work as a career separate from life; make what you love your work.
principles.quote: Make your avocation your vocation. Make what you love your work.

principles.text: The reward is in the journey, not in reaching the pot of gold.
principles.quote: The reward is in the crossing the rainbow.

principles.text: Awareness of mortality motivates you to do something worth leaving behind.
principles.quote: to know my arc will fall makes me want to blaze while I am in the sky.

principles.text: Regrets (what you didn't do) outweigh mistakes; act on your intuitions and dreams.
principles.quote: Regrets are most often things you didn’t do, and wish you did.
